blocks.text: Condo buildings in Maple Ridge
Rosewood Court — 22611 116 Avenue

Built 1991, 81 units. The directory records restrictions as: age restrictions, pets allowed with restrictions, rentals not allowed — the rental line is void since November 24, 2022. Listings describe a 55+ retirement community in Fraserview Village.
Emerald Manor — 11609 227 Street
Built 1997 per current listings, an accessible 55+ retirement community in Fraserview Village; gas and hot water included in the strata fee per listings.
The Willows — 11578 225 Street
Built 1987 per current listings, marketed "for those 55 and better" in Fraserview Village; listings describe it as pet friendly (two cats or two dogs, or one of each).
Castlemount — 11601 227 Street
Listings name it "Castlemount at Fraserview Village," a 55+ community with access to the village clubhouse, exercise facilities, indoor pool and workshop.
Riverside — 11510 225 Street
Built 1988 and described as a 55+ community in a current listing.
Podium — 11655 Fraser Street
Built in 2024, 125 units. Presale information describes a 6-storey wood-frame project by Whitetail Homes with 120 condos and 5 townhomes, which is where the 125 comes from.
Brickwater Village (Brickwater at The Village) — 227 Street / Selkirk Avenue area, by Falcon Homes

A mixed-use project of four buildings, with four storeys of homes over ground-floor shops and "200+ condominiums" in total, according to presale marketing. Listings give the building addresses and years: 22633 Selkirk Avenue (2024), 11865 227 Street (2022), 11893 227 Street (2019) and 22638 119 Avenue (2020).
Highpointe (also spelled "Highpoint" in some listings) — 11641 227 Street
Built 2024; a building-directory listing page records strata plan EPS9270 and the unit as one of 35 units at the address.
Station One — 12070 227 Street
Named in current East Central apartment listings.
Falcon Manor — 22150 Dewdney Trunk Road
Built in 2007, 58 units, by Falcon Homes, according to listings; wood frame, with underground parking.
Era (Era One) — 22265 Dewdney Trunk Road and 22226 Brown Avenue

The first phase of the Era master-planned community, by Johnston Meier Insurance and SwissReal Developments; listings show units built in 2022. Sources differ on the number of condos in Phase 1 (143 or 192). The phase's 49 rental apartments are non-market rentals, not strata condos.
The 222 — 12320 222 Street
A building directory describes a 62-unit wood-frame development with pets allowed.
Canuck Plaza — 12096 222 Street
Named in current West Central apartment listings. Any "25+" age label attached to this building is void: the only lawful strata age bylaw in BC is 55+, so a 25+ line cannot bind a buyer.
Southridge Terrace — 22230 North Avenue
Named in current West Central apartment listings.
Wildwood Terrace — 12170 222 Street
Listings record the complex name as Wildwood Terrace and the property sub-type as Apartment/Condo.
Emerson (The Emerson) — 22315 122 Avenue
Built in 2019, according to listings. A building directory describes a 69-unit concrete development with pets allowed, while one listing says wood frame and mixed construction.
Inspire — 12109, 12133 and 12143 223 Street

By Platinum Group of Companies; a developer/realtor information sheet records Building 3 at 83 homes with an estimated completion of January 2027 — part of this project is presale product (REDMA) — and listings variously record units as built in 2025 and 2026.
Magnolia Gate — 22255 122 Avenue
Named in current West Central apartment listings, which describe underground parking.
223 North — 22318 Lougheed Highway
Named in current West Central apartment listings.
Westbrooke — 12020 207A Street

Listings classify units as Apartment/Condo with Freehold Strata title; a pet-friendly building with a rentable guest suite, elevator, underground parking, and gas and hot water included in the strata fee per listings. Build-year conflict: listings give 2004 and 2005.

items.t: Boundaries: the Fraser River to the south, the Golden Ears range and Golden Ears Provincial Park to the north, Pitt Meadows to the west and Mission to the east.

On MLS®, Maple Ridge is covered by Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and divided into 12 areas: Albion, Cottonwood, East Central, North, Northeast, Northwest, Silver Valley, Southwest, Thornhill, Websters Corners, West Central and Whonnock.

Condos and townhomes in other areas, September 2026 (listed / sold): Albion 18 / 4; Cottonwood 34 / 4; Northwest 5 / 1; Silver Valley 15 / 0; Southwest 8 / 3; Thornhill 8 / 0; North, Northeast, Websters Corners and Whonnock none.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Maple Ridge

items.t: North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan: the Official Community Plan Amending Bylaw was adopted June 23, 2026 (City announcement June 24, 2026), formalizing an approximately 500-acre economic hub in northeast Maple Ridge; the plan establishes future land use designations only and approves no construction or development projects itself.

SSMUH and housing need: based on the City's interim Housing Needs Report, Maple Ridge will need 27,778 new homes by 2041, and the fall 2025 OCP and area-plan updates include new provisions for small-scale multi-unit housing (3 to 6 units on single-detached lots) and increased density around transit hubs. SSMUH product is generally not strata condo product.

blocks.text: Good to know about Maple Ridge condos

items.t: The City's zoning bylaw is No. 7600-2019.

Fraserview Village is a shared-amenity cluster, not four separate worlds. Rosewood Court, Emerald Manor, The Willows, Castlemount and Riverside sit in one 55+ village whose buildings share a village amenity building (indoor pool, hot tub, exercise room/clubhouse, guest suite) described consistently across listings — strata-fee comparisons inside the village have to account for that shared facility.

One project, two tenures, on Dewdney Trunk Road. Era's first phase mixes strata condos with 49 non-market rental apartments in the same phase — a unit's building and tenure, not just its address, decide whether it is a purchasable strata lot at all.

The next OCP cycle is already scheduled. A more comprehensive OCP review, with broad community engagement, is planned following the release of the 2026 Census data and a new Housing Needs Report in 2028, leading up to 2030 — today's plan permissions are a 2025-alignment snapshot, not the final word.

items.t: Plans: Council adopted updates to the Official Community Plan and the Hammond, Silver Valley and Town Centre area plans on November 25, 2025, and updates to the Albion Area Plan on October 28, 2025, to meet the Province's December 31, 2025 deadline for local plans to match provincial housing targets. The Silver Valley Area Plan is part of the Official Community Plan.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Maple Ridge

items.t: Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan: adopted January 27, 2026 (the corridor ends at 221 Street).

Small-scale housing: the City's interim Housing Needs Report says Maple Ridge will need 27,778 new homes by 2041, and the fall 2025 plan updates add small-scale multi-unit housing (3 to 6 units on single detached lots) and more density around transit hubs. So a detached lot's multiplex potential depends on the adopted plan and the zoning bylaw, not a listing's summary.

Next OCP cycle: a more comprehensive OCP review and update, with broad community engagement, is planned following the release of the 2026 Census data and the completion of a new Housing Needs Report in 2028, with the full review leading up to 2030.

For any property in the Agricultural Land Reserve (check the Agricultural Land Commission's maps): subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, and ALR homes can't be stratified. The main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an additional home can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha).

items.t: The usual duplex form: The City's fall 2025 OCP and area-plan updates include new provisions for small-scale multi-unit housing (3 to 6 units on single-detached lots) and increased density around transit hubs, on the City's interim Housing Needs Report figure of 27,778 new homes needed by 2041.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect duplexes in Maple Ridge

items.t: Suites inside a duplex (Maple Ridge): The secondary-suite cap is 40% of gross floor area outside the Floodplain Area — Maple Ridge's own rule, never borrowed.

SSMUH position (Maple Ridge): Duplexes are the baseline form under the provincial SSMUH framework; the City's fall 2025 updates carry SSMUH provisions of 3 to 6 units on single-detached lots with added density around transit hubs.
